newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline still off on APIs but holds support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline still off on APIs but holds support.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline clung to sharply lower levels Wednesday afternoon following news of growing supply, but some traders said gasoline may have seen its lows for the day after holding key technical support.

"The market is definitely down on the APIs, but prices have not totally collapsed, and crude has kept it's backwardation, so we have positive signs," said Jim Fiedler, trader with E. D. & F. Man International Inc.
At 1403 EDT, May gasoline has fallen 1.55 cents at 60.35 cents a gallon, after bouncing off its session low of 60.20 cents early session, above support pegged at 60.00 cents.
The support level is a psychological one and has been breached twice in the last two weeks after being tested several times since late February and holding.

May crude was off 40 cents at $19.43 a barrel, maintaining at three cent backwardation with June even after the American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday that crude grew a larger-than-expected 2.97 million barrels due to imports.
This was the sixth consecutive weekly build in crude.
May heating oil was off 1.50 cents at 53.35 cents a gallon, following a build in distillate stocks when traders had expected a decline.
